? RD-5 rider agreed to this route before the detour; scope of that agreement [F3] RULE: exempt only if a RIDER message sent before 08:42:55 agrees AND the agreement covers this segment. Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. This finding changes the amount. Evidence — F8: Chat #1 08:39 driver: “Traffic ahead on Central Expressway is building up, ok if I go round via Balestier Road?”; F9: Chat #2 08:40 rider: “可以，走 Balestier Road 吧。”; F11: Driver statement (written after the trip, not part of the chat): “I asked the rider before turning off via Balestier Road and the rider agreed.” (F8, F9, F11)

claims.assertion: The trip was a RydeTAXI metered ride (charged $40.45, distance $26.80 for 19.01 km, time $8.17 for 31.4 min per F7), so excess mileage directly increases the fare under RD-2's RydeTAXI branch.

GPS records one off-route segment, 08:42–08:54, where 7.24 km was driven against 2.50 km on the optimal route, adding 4.74 km and reaching up to 1568 m away from that route (F3); nothing exempts it, so it is an unexempted detour segment under RD-1.
The detour is material: actual 19.0 km vs optimal 13.9 km is +5.1 km (+37%), and 31.8 min vs the 20.4 min estimate is +11.4 min (F1, F2).

The only rider consent on record is a named-road authorisation: at 08:40 the rider messaged “可以，走 Balestier Road 吧” in answer to the driver's 08:39 question about going round via Balestier Road (F8, F9), which under RD-5 covers only driving on Balestier Road and does not authorise the whole 08:42–08:54 diversion.

No record ties the driven 08:42–08:54 segment to Balestier Road — the fact table contains no road-name fact for the actual path, only distance and position data (F3, F8, F9) — so on the named-road consent the judge may find the coverage of that segment undetermined (G13), but undetermined consent is not consent and the segment is not exempted under RD-5.

The driver's post-trip statement that the rider agreed (F11) adds nothing: the chat is complete with every message timestamped (F10) and already shows the rider's only words, so the driver's later assertion cannot expand that consent (G11).

The driver cannot invoke the congestion exception: the only congestion evidence is Central Expressway speed band 2 for 08:21–08:42 (F12), which is a band-only record that may at most corroborate an incident (RD-4(b)), and there is no traffic incident at all near the route in the trip window (F15), so RD-4(a) is not satisfied and the segment falls to RD-2.

On the optimal route the neighbouring roads were free-flowing (Ang Mo Kio Ave 8 and Ave 1, band 5, 40–49 km/h, covering 08:21–09:08, F13, F14), which contradicts the driver's premise that the shorter route was impassable and leaves the 4.74 km addition unexplained.

The refund is the unexempted segment's extra kilometres at this trip's per-kilometre rate: 4.74 km × $1.4098/km = $6.68 (F3, F4), the same rate the fare facts use for the billed excess distance of 5.12 km = $7.22 (F4).

The excess billed to the rider exceeds the refund because $7.22 covers 5.12 km while only 4.74 km is attributed to the off-route segment (F1, F3, F4); the remainder is unmatched mileage under RD-2 and is not claimed.

The $0.11 waiting charge is metered in-trip waiting tied to the stops on the detour, not a pickup waiting fee (F5, F7); because the detour segment is unexempted it is a charge arising from that segment and should be waived with it.
The driver has no prior upheld route dispute (0 in 90 days, F18), so the repeat-violation condition of RD-6 is not met and no account flag is requested here.

weaknesses: The rider's 08:40 message (F9) is genuine, timestamped consent given before the 08:42 segment start (F3, F10); the driver will argue it is a route-change authorisation at least for the Balestier Road corridor, which under RD-5 could exempt part or all of the segment.

The off-route segment begins at 08:42, exactly when the Central Expressway speed band 2 window ends (F12), so the driver can argue the band record corroborates a genuine reason to leave the expressway, even though F15 shows no incident and F13/F14 show free flow on the alternatives.

Only one off-route segment is recorded at 4.74 km (F3) while the meter charged $7.22 for 5.12 km of excess (F4); the driver will say the uncovered 0.38 km means the GPS attribution understates the justified mileage, and the refund is capped at the segment figure.

No road-name fact ties the driven path to Balestier Road or to any other road, so if the judge reads the consent as a general route authorisation the whole segment could be exempted (G13), and the complaint's own words ('I'm not sure he took the road he said') concede the rider's uncertainty.

claims.assertion: This is a RydeTAXI metered trip (F7: total $40.45 made up of metered distance/time units plus platform fee), so any route-deviation refund is governed by RD-2's RydeTAXI branch and is limited to the metered distance units of the non-exempt off-route km — not the whole fare difference the rider complains about.

The rider herself, in her own message sent before the detour began, agreed to the named route: Chat #2 at 08:40 reads “可以，走 Balestier Road 吧。” (“OK, let's take Balestier Road”), which is a specific named-road authorization, and the only off-route segment starts at 08:42 (F3), i.e. after that message (F8, F9).

The authorization was sought before the deviation, satisfying Ryde's “mutual agreement before you go” requirement: the driver asked at 08:39 (F8) and the rider consented at 08:40 (F9), both timestamps earlier than the segment start 08:42 in F3.

The driver had a documented traffic reason for the reroute: CENTRAL EXPRESSWAY speed band 2 (10–19 km/h, i.e. severe congestion) during 08:21–08:42 (F12), covering the start of the detour at 08:42, and this is the corridor the driver invoked when he wrote that “Traffic ahead on Central Expressway is building up” (F8).

The congestion band is not a standalone exemption: no LTA DataMall traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window (F15), and RD-4(b) only makes a speed band corroborative evidence, so the driver does not claim exemption on F12 alone.

The consent's scope is limited to the named road and cannot be stretched to the whole 4.74 km of extra distance: the chat names only “Balestier Road” (F9), and nothing in the record ties the driven segment of 08:42–08:54, which strayed up to 1568 m from the optimal route (F3), to Balestier Road — the rider's own complaint says she is “not sure” which road was taken.

As an alternative fallback inside the policy, if the segment is held non-exempt, RD-2's RydeTAXI formula caps the refund at the metered distance units of that segment: the recorded excess is $7.22 (5.12 km × $1.4098/km, F4), calculated from the segment's extra 4.74 km (F3), and the waiting item is only $0.11 for 0.4 min (F5) which stays chargeable under RD-3(c).

There is no fare-side impropriety to add to the refund: no surge applied (multiplier 1.0×, F6), the itemisation shows only base, metered distance, metered time, waiting and the standard $1.47 platform fee with no unpublised add-on (F7), so FARE-1 has nothing to strike out.

The driver's record gives no ground for an account flag: 4.9 years on the platform, 4.61 rating, 1091 trips in 90 days and 0 disputes with 0 upheld (F18), so RD-6's precondition (an earlier upheld route dispute in 90 days) is absent and any refund should not be paired with flag_account.

Neither the chat nor the complaint contains any threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation (F8, F9, F10, F11 — the strongest rider wording is “我不确定他走的是不是他说的那条路”), so this matter should stay on the route/fare track rather than being escalated as a safety event.

weaknesses: RD-1 cuts against the driver on the raw numbers: F1 shows 19.0 km actual vs 13.9 km optimal (+5.1 km, +37%) and F2 shows 31.8 min vs 20.4 min, so the aggregate deviation is large and the driver carries the burden of explaining the whole corridor, not just the 08:42–08:54 segment.

The consent facts (F8, F9) name only “Balestier Road” and there is no fact that ties the driven 08:42–08:54 segment to Balestier Road — the segment wandered up to 1568 m from the optimal route (F3), so the judge may find the consent's reach undetermined under RD-5/G13 and the extra distance not covered.

The driver's own statement “I asked the rider before turning off via Balestier Road and the rider agreed” (F11) adds nothing the chat does not already say and cannot be used to prove a verbal/undocumented consent (G11); it is at best consistent with F8/F9.

On traffic, RD-4 is not fully met: F15 records no LTA traffic incident near the route, and F12 (band 2 on Central Expressway, 08:21–08:42) is, by RD-4(b), only corroborative when it stands alone, so the congestion argument cannot by itself exempt the 4.74 km (F3).
The rider can point to F4 to quantify a concrete monetary harm ($7.22 of excess distance billed) that a court may award under RD-2 even if it accepts the driver's good faith.
